name: loihi_knn_query
description: One approximate k-NN query over a 76,800-pattern database on 32 Loihi chips. Every census number comes from the paper's own structural statements; the energy constants come from a DIFFERENT paper (davies2018loihi Table 2, pre-silicon), so this row is a pre-silicon model predicting an independently measured board. Compared on dynamic energy, which is the column Frady reports separately from static, reset and x86. [E4] The RESET is excluded on both sides deliberately: Frady reports it in its own column, and the pricer would charge it (e_core_init x segment_cores) if this case declared a pass structure — so the census declares none, and the two sides stay composed the same way. Keeping it in would also have made the row partly self-consistent, since e_core_init is derived from that very Reset column.

census_sources.cores_physical: davies2018loihi p.95: 128 neuromorphic cores per chip x 32 chips
census_sources.neurons_physical: davies2018loihi: 1024 compartments per core x 128 cores x 32 chips
census_sources.neurons_used: frady2020neuromorphic S3: one pattern-match neuron per database pattern, 76,800 patterns
census_sources.timesteps: frady2020neuromorphic S3: 'the window length is T = 60 timesteps'
census_sources.synaptic_events: frady2020neuromorphic S3: W = [E, -E] gives 2 x 500 = 1000 input components; 'The used setting theta_e = 0.1 typically removes about one quarter to one third of spikes' -> 708 transmitted (midpoint of 667-750); 'Each input spike is broadcast to all pattern match neurons' -> x 76,800
census_sources.macs: one synaptic event is one MAC on an event-driven chip
census_sources.segment_cores: every core of the 32 chips is configured for the search
census_sources.sync_count: barrier sync is per timestep and already inside the measured window
census_sources.host_macs: the x86 share is measured separately by the paper and excluded here
census_sources.host_ops_s: the x86 share is measured separately by the paper and excluded here
